title: xfeeds: an independence-aware public threat intelligence feed
description:
xfeeds is a self-updating, open threat intelligence pipeline that collects, normalizes, enriches, scores, filters, and publishes malicious-IP indicators in CSV, JSON, STIX 2.1, MISP, and firewall rule sets. A GitHub Actions pipeline targets six-hour refreshes and publishes a dashboard through GitHub Pages; scheduling is best-effort.

Most public blocklists mirror or re-derive one another. xfeeds models that dependency explicitly:

  • Independence classes. Only the strongest contribution within each source family counts, so mirrored lists cannot vote twice.
  • Freshness gating. Successful fetches do not establish evidence freshness. Stale evidence cannot admit records; expired or dormant evidence casts no vote.
  • Redistribution-aware tiering. Restricted sources may corroborate already-admitted records without exposing restricted source identities in public records. Primary, noncommercial, and clean-provenance tiers preserve distinct redistribution terms.
  • Conservative admission. Publication normally requires two fresh redistributable classes. Configured, verified Spamhaus DROP sources have a single-source promotion exception. Benign-scanner evidence caps confidence rather than deleting records.

This deposit archives software, not a feed dataset. Generated feeds, the legacy dataset, and recorded upstream-response fixture payloads are excluded. The MIT licence covers the software. For the complete fixture-based test suite, use the corresponding GitHub tag. Design decisions, source methodology, and licence research are recorded under docs/.
